appearance.languageHint: The language Chip Hippo's own menus, panels and dialogs are shown in. The user guide is only available in English.
appearance.fontSizeHint: The size of text in Chip Hippo's own toolbars, panels and dialogs, in pixels. Part and board markings on the desk belong to the circuit, so they scale with the desk zoom instead.
appearance.wireLayoutHint: How a new wire is drawn: Direct sags from hole to hole; Routed runs straight, and can be bent around the board by dragging points into it. Wires already on the desk keep the layout they have — change one through its own Properties dialog.
appearance.trayAutoCloseHint: When this is on, opening a folder in the parts tray closes every other folder, so only the one you're working in stays open — along with the folder it sits inside. Clicking an icon on the shut tray's strip does the same.
appearance.view3dHint: Shows the 3D view button in the toolbar, for looking at the desk in three dimensions; Off hides it. The 3D view needs WebGL.

datasheets.familyHint: Which logic family the parts tray shows: the 74LS TTL chips, the CD4000 CMOS chips, or both — each in a folder of its own. It only filters the tray: a project's chips always load and run whatever is chosen here, and a family the open project uses is shown anyway, so you can add more of the parts already on its desk.
datasheets.folderHint: Point this at a folder of manufacturer datasheet PDFs named after each chip (e.g. 74LS00.pdf). When a matching PDF is found, a chip's pin-assignments window shows a button to open it.
datasheets.downloadTitle: Download datasheets into the app's own folder
datasheets.autoHint: Downloads a datasheet for every part Chip Hippo has a published source on file for — the manufacturer's own document where there is one, otherwise a reference library — into Chip Hippo's own folder, and points the setting above at it. Parts with no source are skipped, and files already there are replaced.

ai.hint: Chip Hippo uses your own connection — nothing is sent anywhere until you ask it to build something, and the key is stored encrypted by the operating system, never in settings.json. Leave Base URL and Model blank to use the shown defaults.
ai.experimental: AI generation is experimental. Every design is verified against the simulator before it is offered, but it may not be the most optimal circuit or the tidiest layout — expect to review and adjust it.

spice.enabledHint: Runs the circuit on Spice Lite, a more electrical simulation: node voltages, charging capacitors, current limits and supply droop. Off uses the standard logic-level engine. A change takes effect the next time you press Run.
spice.gapHint: When a voltage counts as having arrived: once the gap left to its final value is under this share of the step it is taking. 1 % is about five time constants. It only decides how long the probe keeps redrawing the voltage — it never holds the circuit up.

source.74LS: Typical values from TI's SN74LS00 datasheet.
source.CD4000: Typical values from TI's CD4001B datasheet, at 5 V. Delay and thresholds scale with each chip's supply.

review.noSupply: There is no power supply on the desk, so nothing can run. Add one from the parts tray and wire it to the board's power rails.
review.unpowered: {ref} ({id}) is wired but never reaches a supply — its VCC/GND nets carry no power.

outputsDisabledUnwired.one: {chip} drives nothing: its active-low output enable {pin} is not wired at all, and an unwired input reads HIGH. Tie it to GND.
outputsDisabledUnwired.other: {chip} drives nothing: its active-low output enables {pin} are not wired at all, and an unwired input reads HIGH. Tie them to GND.

outputsDisabledHigh.one: {chip} is switched off right now: its active-low output enable {pin} is HIGH, so its outputs float. Drive it LOW to enable them.
outputsDisabledHigh.other: {chip} is switched off right now: its active-low output enables {pin} are HIGH, so its outputs float. Drive them LOW to enable them.

outputsDisabledUnwiredActiveHigh.one: {chip}'s outputs are not enabled: its active-high output enable {pin} is not wired at all. Tie it HIGH.
outputsDisabledUnwiredActiveHigh.other: {chip}'s outputs are not enabled: its active-high output enables {pin} are not wired at all. Tie them HIGH.

outputsDisabledLow.one: {chip} is switched off right now: its active-high output enable {pin} is LOW, so its outputs float. Drive it HIGH to enable them.
outputsDisabledLow.other: {chip} is switched off right now: its active-high output enables {pin} are LOW, so its outputs float. Drive them HIGH to enable them.

review.inputFloating: {ref} ({id}) has inputs nothing drives: {pins}. A floating TTL input reads HIGH, so the chip works — just not as designed. Tie each one to VCC or GND, or wire it to whatever should drive it.
review.inputFloatingCmos: {ref} ({id}) has inputs nothing drives: {pins}. A floating CMOS input reads neither HIGH nor LOW, so what the chip does is anybody's guess. Tie every input to VCC or GND — spare gates included — or wire it to whatever should drive it.
review.busFight: {drivers} are wired to the same net ({net}). Two outputs must never share a net — one drives HIGH while the other drives LOW and they fight.
review.ledUnlimited: {ref} ({id}) is conducting with nothing limiting the current — on a real bench it would burn out rather than light. Put a resistor in series with it.
review.diodeUnlimited: {ref} ({id}) is forward-biased straight across two strongly driven nets — rail to rail, or an output into a rail — with nothing limiting the current. On a real bench it would burn out, or take the output with it. Put a resistor in series with it.

reason.transistor: is left out: Digital has no transistor that switches as this one does

oscillationMessage.one: The circuit won't settle ({count} unstable net).
oscillationMessage.other: The circuit won't settle ({count} unstable nets).

sim.underpoweredMessage: {chip} is at {volts} V, below the {rating} it needs — running inert.
sim.damagedMessage: {chip} was damaged by {volts} V — it is rated for {rating}. Stopping the simulation restores it.

floatingInputMessage.one: {chip} has nothing driving pin {pins}. A floating CMOS input reads neither HIGH nor LOW — tie every input, spare gates included.
floatingInputMessage.other: {chip} has nothing driving pins {pins}. A floating CMOS input reads neither HIGH nor LOW — tie every input, spare gates included.

sim.marginalHighMessage: A 74LS output drives a CD4000 input on {net}. Its HIGH (about 3.4 V) is below the 3.5 V a CMOS input needs at 5 V — add a pull-up resistor to VCC.

lsFanoutMessage.one: {chip} drives {loads} 74LS inputs on {net}, but can only hold {count} LOW. Buffer it with a CD4049UB or CD4050B.
lsFanoutMessage.other: {chip} drives {loads} 74LS inputs on {net}, but can only hold {count} LOW. Buffer it with a CD4049UB or CD4050B.

sim.mixedSupplyMessage: {net} joins chips powered at {volts}. A signal crossing between supplies needs a level shifter.
sim.shortThroughTransistorMessage: Opposing supplies meet through a transistor that is switched on ({net}) — nothing limits the current.

brownoutMessage.one: {chip} pin {pin} is driving {level}, but its load holds the net at {volts} V — {count} input on it does not read {level}. The output cannot hold that many inputs, or a load that heavy.
brownoutMessage.other: {chip} pin {pin} is driving {level}, but its load holds the net at {volts} V — {count} inputs on it do not read {level}. The output cannot hold that many inputs, or a load that heavy.

sim.overloadedMessage: {chip} let the brown smoke out: it was pushed past its absolute maximum rating. Stopping the simulation restores it.
sim.supplySpikeMessage: {psu} is asked for {peak} mA as chips switch together — past its {limit} mA limit. A 100 nF capacitor across the rails next to the chips supplies those spikes.
sim.ledBurntMessage: {led} burnt out: {current} mA would heat its junction to {tj} °C, past its {max} °C maximum. Stopping the simulation restores it.
sim.diodeBurntMessage: {diode} burnt out: {current} mA would heat its junction to {tj} °C, past its {max} °C maximum — nothing limits the current through it. Stopping the simulation restores it.
sim.outputCurrentMessage: {chip} pin {pin} is carrying {current} mA — more than the {limit} mA its output is made for.
sim.outputCurrentSmokeMessage: {chip} let the brown smoke out: pin {pin} carried {current} mA, past the {limit} mA its output survives. Stopping the simulation restores it.
sim.outputPowerMessage: {chip} pin {pin} is dissipating {power} mW in its output — more than the {limit} mW it is made for.
sim.outputPowerSmokeMessage: {chip} let the brown smoke out: pin {pin} dissipated {power} mW in its output, past the {limit} mW it survives. Stopping the simulation restores it.
sim.rxCurrentMessage: {chip} pin {pin}: its discharge transistor is holding {current} mA — more than the {limit} mA a timing resistor of at least {rxMin} kΩ, the least its datasheet allows, would let through.
sim.inputOvervoltageMessage: {chip} let the brown smoke out: pin {pin} was held at {volts} V, past the {max} V a 74LS input survives. Stopping the simulation restores it.
sim.inputClampMessage: {chip} pin {pin} is held at {volts} V, outside its supply: its protection diode is carrying {current} mA.
sim.inputClampSmokeMessage: {chip} let the brown smoke out: pin {pin} was held at {volts} V, and its protection diode carried {current} mA, past the {max} mA it survives. Stopping the simulation restores it.
sim.switchCurrentMessage: {chip} is passing {current} mA through a switch — more than the {limit} mA its switches are rated for.
sim.switchCurrentSmokeMessage: {chip} let the brown smoke out: a switch carried {current} mA, past the {limit} mA it survives. Stopping the simulation restores it.
sim.transistorCurrentMessage: {part} is carrying {current} mA — more than the {limit} mA a transistor like it is made for.
sim.transistorPowerMessage: {part} is dissipating {power} mW — more than the {limit} mW its package is made for.
sim.transistorCurrentSmokeMessage: {part} is carrying {current} mA, past the {limit} mA a transistor like it survives — a real one would have failed.
sim.transistorPowerSmokeMessage: {part} is dissipating {power} mW, past the {limit} mW its package survives — a real one would have failed.
sim.inductiveKickMessage: {part} broke down at {volts} V: an inductor's current had nowhere else to go, and dumped {energy} mJ into it. A diode across the coil would carry it.
sim.clockUnpoweredMessage: {clock} has no power, so it is not ticking. Wire its vcc terminal to the + rail and its gnd terminal to the − rail; its HIGH is that supply's voltage.
sim.ledOverdrivenMessage: {led} is carrying {current} mA, past its {rating} mA rating — bright, but it will not last. A larger series resistor brings it back within its rating.
sim.ledReverseMessage: {led} has {volts} V across it backwards, past the {rating} V its datasheet allows.

warning.unpowered: Unpowered — no supply reaches VCC and GND, so this part computes nothing.
warning.underpowered: Underpowered — VCC is at {volts} V, below the {rating} this part needs, so it runs inert.
warning.reversed: Power reversed — VCC and GND are swapped.
warning.damaged: Damaged — {volts} V is over this part's {rating}, and it let the smoke out. Stopping the simulation restores it.
warning.unprogrammed: Not programmed — no image is loaded, so this chip reads random noise.
warning.timing: Timing not recognised — {problems}. Its outputs stay at rest until it is wired as its datasheet shows.
warning.heldOn: Holding ON — its gate reads no level, and the charge left on it keeps the channel conducting. A real gate leaks that charge away, so tie it to a defined level with a resistor.
warning.heldOff: Holding OFF — its gate reads no level, so it stays as it was last driven (off, if its gate has not been driven yet). A real gate drifts, so tie it to a defined level with a resistor.
warning.overloaded: Overloaded — an output was asked for twice the current it is rated for, or more, and it let the brown smoke out. Stopping the simulation restores it.

run.signature: The code on “{name}” was built for a different design. Generate it again and put it back on the board.
run.version: “{name}” speaks protocol v{device}; Chip Hippo speaks v{host}. Generate its code again and put it back on the board.
run.dropped: The serial connection to “{name}” was dropped, so the circuit has stopped.
run.delivery: Delivery to “{name}” failed after {attempts} attempts, so the circuit has stopped. Is its sketch calling ChipHippo.poll() often enough?
run.noResponse: Nothing answered on {port} for “{name}”. Is the sketch uploaded, and does it call ChipHippo.begin() and ChipHippo.poll()?
run.restart: “{name}” left the run — it restarted, or stopped hearing Chip Hippo — so the circuit has stopped. Run it again to reconnect.

faultTitle.drop-ack: Swallow the acknowledgement of the next Output, so Chip Hippo times out and sends it again
faultTitle.corrupt: Damage the next acknowledgement or Input the Mock sends, so Chip Hippo asks for it again

faultTitle.wrong-signature: Answer the next Run as a sketch built for another design, so it refuses to start

diag.unterminatedComment: This /* comment is never closed with */.
diag.escapedIdentifier: Escaped identifiers (\name) are not supported — use a plain name.
diag.realNumber: Real numbers are not supported — every value here is a whole number of bits.
diag.unexpectedEnd: The code ends in the middle of a statement.
diag.systemTask: System tasks like {name} are not supported — the debugger's watch panel shows every value.
diag.directive: Compiler directives like {name} are not supported.
diag.signedUnsupported: signed is not supported — use integer for a signed 32-bit value.
diag.functionCall: Calling {name}(…) is not supported — functions are not part of this subset.
diag.keywordInExpression: '{word}' is a Verilog keyword and cannot be used in an expression.
diag.keywordAsName: '{word}' is a Verilog keyword, so it cannot be a name.
diag.expectedTarget: Expected something to assign to, but found '{found}'.
diag.delayUnsupported: Delays (#) are not supported — Chip Hippo's chips are zero-delay.
diag.eventInStatement: An event control (@) can only start an always block.
diag.declarationInBlock: Declare {word} variables at the top, or give the block a name (begin : name) to declare them inside it.
diag.declarationAfterStatement: Declare {word} variables at the start of the block, before its statements.
diag.declarationAtTop: Declare {word} at the top of the module, not inside begin…end.
diag.blockInitialiser: {name} is declared in a block, so it can't be given a value there — set it with a statement.
diag.duplicateBlockName: There is already a block named {name} here.
diag.duplicateDefault: A case may have only one default.
diag.taskCall: Calling {name}(…) is not supported — tasks are not part of this subset.
diag.headerInBody: The module header is generated from the package — write only the body, with no module or endmodule.
diag.portInBody: Pins are declared by the generated header — set them in the package, not with {word}.
diag.realUnsupported: {word} is not supported — values here are bits.
diag.functionUnsupported: {word} is not supported — write the logic out where it is used.
diag.unsupportedConstruct: {word} is not supported in a custom chip.
diag.netTypeUnsupported: {word} nets are not supported — use wire.
diag.gateUnsupported: Gate primitives such as {word} are not supported — write an assign instead.
diag.arrayUnsupported: Arrays of wires are not supported — declare the array as reg (or integer).
diag.arrayInitialiser: An array can't be given a value where it is declared — fill {name} from an initial block.
diag.wholeArray: {name} is an array — read or write one word at a time, as {name}[index].
diag.memoryTooDeep: {name} holds {depth} words; an array may hold at most {max}.
diag.memoryTooLarge: The arrays here hold {total} words in all; a chip may hold at most {max}.
diag.memoryInComb: {name} is an array, so only an always @(posedge …) or initial block may set it — set from always @(*) it would be a latch.
diag.alwaysNeedsEvent: An always block needs an event control: @(*) or @(posedge …).
diag.instanceUnsupported: Module instances are not supported — a custom chip is one module (use units to repeat it).
diag.expectedItem: Expected a declaration, assign, always or initial, but found '{found}'.
diag.edgeUnsupported: 'edge' is not supported — use posedge or negedge.
diag.loopUnsupported: {word} loops are not supported — a loop here must have constant bounds, so use for or repeat.
diag.loopHeaderDeclaration: Declaring the counter in the for (…) is SystemVerilog — declare it first, at the top or in a named block (begin : name integer i; …).
diag.loopCounterForm: A for loop sets one counter in its first and last parts, such as for (i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1).
diag.loopNotStatic: A loop's bounds must be constants — numbers and parameters, and in its condition and step the counter itself — so that it always finishes.
diag.loopCounterAssigned: The loop's own counter {name} is set inside it, so how often it runs can't be known.
diag.loopTooLong: This loop runs more than {max} times, or never ends — a loop here may run at most {max} times.
diag.loopCounterShared: {name} counts a loop in more than one always block — declare a counter inside each block (begin : name integer i; …).
diag.proceduralAssign: {word} inside a block is not supported — use = or <=.
diag.badSize: A number's size must be at least 1.
diag.tooWide: That is {width} bits wide; a value may be at most {max}.
diag.badDigit: This number has a digit its base does not allow.
diag.numberTooBig: That number does not fit in 32 bits.
diag.outputRedeclared: {name} is an output pin — the generated header declares it (as output reg when an always block drives it), so do not declare it again.
diag.inputRedeclared: {name} is an input pin — the generated header declares it.
diag.inoutRedeclared: {name} is an inout pin — the generated header declares it.
diag.unknownConstant: This constant has x or z bits.
diag.undeclared: {name} is not declared — declare it with wire or reg, or add it as a pin.
diag.notConstant: {name} is not a constant — only numbers and parameters can go here.
diag.selectOfParameter: Part-selects of a parameter are not supported.
diag.reversedSelect: This range runs the opposite way to {name}'s declaration.
diag.badSelectWidth: The width after +: or -: must be a constant from 1 to {max}.
diag.unsizedInConcat: A number inside { } needs a size, such as 4'd3.
diag.badReplication: A replication count must be at least 1.
diag.assignToParameter: {name} is a parameter, so it cannot be assigned.
diag.assignToInput: {name} is an input pin, so it cannot be assigned.
diag.assignToReg: {name} is a reg — assign drives wires; set a reg inside an always block.
diag.mixedDrivers: {name} is driven both by assign and by an always or initial block.
diag.multipleDrivers: {name} is driven by more than one assign.
diag.proceduralToWire: {name} is a wire — an always block can only set a reg.
diag.inoutProcedural: {name} is an inout pin — drive it with assign (giving z where it lets go), not from an always or initial block.
diag.multipleAlwaysDrivers: {name} is set in more than one always block.
diag.mixedSensitivity: An event list cannot mix edges (posedge, negedge) with plain signals.
diag.latch: {name} is not set on every path through this always @(*), which would make a latch. Give it a value first, or cover every case.
diag.nonblockingReadBack: {name} is set with <= and then read in the same combinational block, where it still holds its old value — set it with = in always @(*).
diag.assignVariableSelect: {name} is assigned at a bit chosen by a variable — assign drives a fixed bit or range; choose the bit inside an always @(*) block.
diag.sensitivityNotName: Name plain signals in this event list.
diag.incompleteSensitivity: This block reads {names}, which its event list leaves out — use @(*).
diag.edgeNotInput: Only an input pin can clock an always block.
diag.edgeNeedsBit: {name} is several bits wide — clock from one bit of it, such as {name}[0].
diag.clockAmbiguous: Which of these signals is the clock is unclear — test each asynchronous control in the block's leading if.
diag.multipleClocks: A module has one clock, but {first} and {second} both clock blocks here. Put logic on another clock in another chip.
diag.outputUndriven: Output {name} is never driven, so it floats (z).
diag.regUnassigned: {name} is never set, so it stays x.
diag.combLoop: Combinational loop: {names}. assign and always @(*) cannot hold state — use an always @(posedge …) block.
diag.badPortName: {name} cannot be a pin name in Verilog — use letters, digits and _, starting with a letter.
